title: The issuer declares `protected_resources` and leaves it empty
rationale: An empty array is a declared member that enumerates nothing, so RFC 9728 7.6's cross-check stays exactly as impossible as if the member were absent -- and counting it as "publishes" inflated C18, R11.1's rank-2 headline candidate. That defect was found by running the code on 29 July 2026 and fixed with no fixture to hold it down, which is how it would come back: `if isinstance(resources, list)` is the natural way to write this check and it is the wrong way. The empty case is still counted separately as `empty_list`, because "declared the member and left it empty" is a different observation from "never declared it" and the difference is worth a number in its own right.

spec.quote:
protected_resources
      OPTIONAL.  JSON array containing a list of resource identifiers for OAuth protected resources that can be used with this authorization server.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 28 July 2026. "a list of resource identifiers" is what an empty array does not contain.

spec.quote: Secure determination of appropriate authorization servers to use with a protected resource for all use cases is out of scope for this specification.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org; the cross-check an empty list cannot serve
